Favor insurers (LIFE, ABDA) and niche lenders (INPC) for structural upside, as US weakness rotates capital into ID defensives. Trim any exposure to BEKS/WIDI on liquidity risk.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's downstream mineral export ban policy continues to structurally reprice domestic smelters and miners, favoring integrated players like CUAN and TINS with captive ore supply.
Global energy transition demand for copper and tin remains a durable multi-year driver, with Indonesia's resource nationalism tightening supply chains and supporting price floors.
The sector's low aggregate beta to US energy moves, given IDX's domestic demand base, creates recurring alpha from idiosyncratic catalysts like SMMT/SURE listings and corporate actions.
sectors.ai: Buy SMMT and SURE on follow-through momentum post-listing/restructuring catalysts, but take profits into strength given aggregate sector signal is NORMAL and US energy weakness caps upside. Rotate into TINS and CUAN for tin/copper supply tightness exposure as Indonesia export restrictions bite. Avoid chasing SQMI/ITMA one-day spikes without volume confirmation.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's energy transition hinges on PLN's grid integration and tariff reform, making utility-linked names (CDIA) more durable than volatile equipment makers.
US nuclear and regulated utilities (CEG, VST) benefit from AI-driven power demand and clean-firm credits, a structural bid independent of Indonesian policy.
Hydrogen and fuel-cell equities (PLUG) remain policy-dependent and high-beta; expect continued divergence from cash-generative renewable operators in both markets.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesia renewables exposure on pullbacks, but rotate toward US nuclear/utility names (CEG, VST) for near-term alpha; PKPK's spike is speculative, not fundamental. Favor names with contracted cash flows over hydrogen/equipment plays. Add on weakness in NRG/CDIA if IDR stabilizes.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's consumer sector outperformance vs US reflects resilient domestic purchasing power and lower import-cost pass-through, favoring local brands over multinationals.
Mid-cap FMCG names with niche categories (health, personal care, snacks) are gaining share from giants via agile innovation and digital distribution, a durable structural shift.
Government social-spending and minimum-wage hikes sustain rural and lower-tier urban consumption, underpinning volume growth for mass-market consumer goods into 2025.
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap consumer names showing idiosyncratic momentum (PPRI, FOLK, EURO) while large-cap staples lag; the ID/US divergence signals domestic resilience. Rotate into local-demand plays with pricing power and distribution reach, avoid US-exposed FMCG. Watch for pullbacks in +9-16% movers to add, as sector breadth remains narrow but supportive.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's pending crypto exchange and clearing house mandate will structurally favor compliant, high-liquidity tokens listed on local platforms, driving sustained institutional inflows.
AI-crypto convergence (TAO, NEAR) is a durable multi-year driver as decentralized compute demand rises, independent of retail sentiment swings.
Privacy coins (ZEC, DASH) face recurring regulatory overhang in Indonesia's strict AML framework, capping upside despite periodic technical rallies.
sectors.ai: Rotate into AI-infrastructure and privacy plays (TAO, NEAR, ZEC) over generic L1s; ARB/JUP spikes are liquidity-driven and mean-reverting. Trim DOT/DASH into strength. Hold cash for a pullback to re-enter at support; Indonesia's regulatory clarity favors compliant tokens—prioritize those with local exchange listings.
